title: Canonical section maps for directed colimits
statement: Canonical section maps for directed colimits.

proof.text: For each open U, evaluate the sheaf colimit cocone at U. Its point is (colimit D)(U), and its legs are the component maps of colimit.ι D i. Apply colimit.desc to this cocone of sets. The coprojection equation colimit.ι_desc gives the required formula for every section. No sheafification or directedness argument is needed.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $D:J\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram admitting a colimit and let $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor such that
$G\circ D$ admits a colimit. There is a canonical morphism

$$
\operatorname{colim}_{j}G(D_j)\longrightarrow G\bigl(\operatorname{colim}_jD_j\bigr)
$$

whose composite with the $j$-th coprojection of $\operatorname{colim}_jG(D_j)$ is $G$ applied to the $j$-th
coprojection $D_j\to\operatorname{colim}_jD_j$, for every $j\in J$. In particular, for a diagram $D$ of sheaves on
a topological space $X$ and an open $U\subseteq X$, taking $G$ to be the sections over $U$ gives a canonical map
$\operatorname{colim}_jD_j(U)\to(\operatorname{colim}_jD_j)(U)$ sending the class of $s\in D_j(U)$ to the image of
$s$ under the $U$-component of the $j$-th coprojection.

proof.text:
Apply $G$ to the colimit cocone of $D$. This is a cocone over $G\circ D$ with point $G(\operatorname{colim}_jD_j)$ and
legs $G$ of the coprojections. The universal property of $\operatorname{colim}_jG(D_j)$ gives the unique morphism out of
it compatible with these legs, which is the required formula. For sheaves, $G$ is evaluation at $U$. No
sheafification or directedness argument is needed.
